canvas-01.description: The north-east side of Hampton, drawn at 100 feet to an inch in the lower half of Sheet 1, below the key map, index and title. The sheet is turned on the page: north points to the upper left (the needle is drawn about 65 degrees anticlockwise from straight up). Hill Street enters at the upper left and turns east to meet Smith Street, which runs off to the north-east; Lackawanna Street runs down the left side towards the railroad. The middle of the part is taken up by the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad and the Central Railroad of New Jersey, drawn as bundles of tracks crossing diagonally, with a turntable, coal pockets, a hand car house and the D.L.& W. freight and passenger station beside a platform. North-west of the tracks stands the Standard Water System Co. works, makers of water stills, a concrete block building with machine shops, an engine house, gas and acid houses and an oil house. South-east of the tracks, along Railroad Avenue, East Grand Street and Church Street, are the Lackawanna House and Hampton House hotels, St. Ann's Roman Catholic Church with its rectory, a cemetery, dwellings, an auto repair shop and a gasoline tank. Main Street and New Street begin at Church Street at the bottom edge, and Foss Avenue at the lower right. Most of the land north of the railroads is divided into large, sparsely built lots (blocks 9, 10, 11 and 15); a dash-dot line at the bottom marks the match with Sheet 2, and the borough limit crosses the right side.
notes: Turned on the page; the drawn needle is about 10 degrees anticlockwise of the fitted north (about -55 degrees), consistent with magnetic north in 1921.
Church St. east of Main St. is Main Street today; Main St. at its north end is realigned (the junction is about 11 m from the modern node).
Hill and Smith Streets are cut through by NJ 31 today; their junction lies about 17 m from the modern Johnson Avenue / NJ 31 node through this placement (not used as control).
Railroads: D.L.& W. R.R. (with station) and C.R.R. of N.J.; neither is in the modern railway extract.

Placed (helmert) from three points: East Grand / Church and Foss / Main carried from sheet 3, and Lackawanna Street over the former D.L.& W. line hand-picked at the left edge; fit RMSE 7.8 m, low confidence.

Sheet 1, 100 ft. Upper half: title, key map (not to scale for georeferencing), index and water/fire notes; lower half: map of the north-east side (Hill, Smith, Lackawanna Sts, the D.L.&W. and C.R.R. of N.J. yards, Church St), turned with north to the upper left. One part. Hill/Smith area rebuilt around NJ 31; placed from two junctions carried from sheet 3 (low confidence).

sheet-2-1.description: The west side of Hampton, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. Main Street runs diagonally across the sheet from the railroad at the right edge to the south-west corner, where it turns west and Asbury Road branches off to the south. Lackawana Street (also named Bridge) crosses the top right to Railroad Avenue, which runs down the right edge beside the Central Railroad of New Jersey; Bowlby Street and Conley Lane lie between them, and Skillman Street, John Street, a lane and Baylor Avenue lie south-east of Main Street. The blocks along Main Street are closely built with frame dwellings, stores and the Baptist Church, with a cemetery behind it and the Presbyterian chapel further west; north of Main Street the land is divided into long, sparsely built lots (blocks 12 and 13). Industry is concentrated at the railroad: the Plainfield Milk and Cream Co. creamery at the top right, E.P. Baylor's coal and lumber yard with lumber sheds beside Railroad Avenue, and a bakery and garage at the Main Street crossing. The Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad crosses the upper left. The left third of the sheet, beyond a heavy line, is a separate map of Old Hampton (part 2). Water pipes, hydrants and street widths are marked.
notes: Lackawana (Bridge) is spelled with one n on this sheet; Lackawanna Street today.

Skillman is Lower Skillman Street today; John (west of Lane) is Riddle Avenue; Baylor Av. is John Street; the lane north of Skillman is Lake Street; Asbury Rd is Valley Road at its junction with Main Street.
Conley Lane is not matched to a modern street; NJ 31 now crosses the north part of the sheet.
Fit residuals of 3 to 8 m at every junction (leave-one-out about 10 m): medium-low confidence.

Sheet 2, 100 ft, two parts divided by a heavy line: part 1 Hampton west of the railroad (Main, Lackawana (Bridge), Bowlby, Skillman, John, Baylor Av., Railroad), turned north to the upper left; part 2 Old Hampton (Main, Washington Rd, Musconetcong River, Adler Lanes Shoddy Mill), located 1 1/4 miles N.W. of the town hall, north up.

sheet-2-2.description: Old Hampton, a small mill settlement on the Musconetcong River about a mile and a quarter north-west of Hampton's town hall, drawn as a separate map at 100 feet to an inch in the left third of Sheet 2, divided from the Hampton map by a heavy line and drawn with north up. Main Street runs down the middle of the part, lined on both sides by a thin row of frame dwellings with stables, milk houses and auto houses, several of them marked old, and a public school (no heat, no lights) near the top. A road leaves Main Street westward past the Adler Lanes Shoddy Mill (not in operation, power by water, no watchman), crossing a mill channel on a stone bridge and the river itself on an iron bridge to Washington Road on the far bank, where a few more dwellings and a milk house stand. The Musconetcong River divides around an island with a dam and the ruins of an older building. The rest of the part is open land (blocks 25, 26 and 27), with the edge marked no exposure. A note under the title states that there is no fire apparatus.
notes: Main (Old Hampton) is taken to be Musconetcong River Road; the road to the iron bridge is Shoddy Mill Road; Washington Rd is probably Rymon Road (Warren County side).

Placed from one hand-picked junction (Musconetcong River Road / Shoddy Mill Road) and a point 349 m south along Musconetcong River Road matched to the drawn Main Street: the rotation rests on the assumption that the road is on its old line (it comes out 11 degrees from the drawn needle). The Washington Rd junction lands 42 m from the modern Rymon Road node: low confidence, errors of tens of metres possible.
Not in Hampton borough; the label says located 1 1/4 miles N.W. of the town hall.

Sheet 2, 100 ft, two parts divided by a heavy line: part 1 Hampton west of the railroad (Main, Lackawana (Bridge), Bowlby, Skillman, John, Baylor Av., Railroad), turned north to the upper left; part 2 Old Hampton (Main, Washington Rd, Musconetcong River, Adler Lanes Shoddy Mill), located 1 1/4 miles N.W. of the town hall, north up.

sheet-3.description: The centre and east side of Hampton between the Central Railroad of New Jersey and Foss Avenue, from Church Street south to Skillman Street, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. Main Street crosses diagonally from the railroad crossing at the left to Church Street at the top. The business centre lies along it near East Grand Street: the fire house and town hall, a drug store, the post office, a barber, a cobbler and confectioners, and a building with general store, motion pictures and lodge rooms. East Grand Street, West Grand Street, Wells Avenue and New Street run down the sheet, crossed by Elk Street and Skillman Street, and are lined with frame dwellings on narrow lots; the M.E. Church stands on Wells Avenue below Elk Street. East of New Street the land between Church Street and Foss Avenue is mostly open (block 24) apart from the Hampton Public School, a brick building, and blocks 1 and 23 beyond Foss Avenue (marked not opened) are empty except for the borough limits crossing them. Along the railroad on the left are Railroad Avenue, coal pockets, the turntable, and at the lower left Baylor Avenue with sheds. South Street runs off the bottom edge. Water pipes, hydrants and street widths (30 to 55 feet) are marked.
notes: Elk is South Street today; Skillman is Upper Skillman Street (with Charlestown Road leaving it at New Street); Church east of Main is Main Street today.
Fit RMSE 3.4 m, leave-one-out 4.4 m from 15 detected junctions.

Sheet 3, 100 ft. Centre and east side: Main, Church, E. and W. Grand, Wells Av., New, Elk (= South Street), Foss Av., Skillman (= Upper Skillman Street); turned north to the upper left. One part; 15 junctions detected.
